newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Technical woes create chaos on German bourse.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Technical woes create chaos on German bourse.

text.p: All floor trade in equities, bonds and derivatives was temporarily suspended as the markets were roaring ahead on Wednesday because of massive system problems, the German bourse said.
Electronic trade on the IBIS computerised trading system was also interrupted, but dealing on the DTB futures exchange was undisturbed, the bourse said.
"All trading in Frankfurt and the nation's regional bourses has been temporarily suspended due to system problems," a bourse spokesman told Reuters.
Sources at the exchange said the hitch stemmed from a system overload.
The shutdown was the second time this week that bourse trading has been interrupted due to technical problems.

German stocks and bonds market were racing higher as business was halted at around 1015 GMT, with the DAX index of 30-leading shares up 164.57 at 493.44 and IBIS DAX index of electronic trade up 105.06 points at 4,402.70. Earlier, the DAX index had hit a new all-time high at 4,418.64 points.
A key speech on the U.S. economy, delivered by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan late on Tuesday, was behind the gains, traders said.

While Greenspan said that interest rates might have to rise in the U.S. to curb price pressure, he suggested that a monetary tightening was not imminent, analysts said, boosting Wall Street and the dollar.

When German floor trade was resumed at 1115 GMT, both bond and stock markets continued to trade in firm ground. Floor trade, which usually runs until around 1130 GMT, was be extended on Wednesday to close at 1230 to compensate for the loss of dealing time due to the shutdwon, the bourse said.

A bourse spokesman told Reuters that the computerised IBIS trading system was being tested and would resume full trade at 1245 GMT. The exchange had hoped to get full electronic trade restarted earlier, but then decided to continue testing the computerised system until floor trade had closed.
"We want to wait until floor trade is closed (to restart full trade on the IBIS system)," the spokesman told Reuters.

By 1240 GMT, the DAX share index had closed a hefty 4.15 percent higher on the day 4,406.09, up 175.67 points. In the debt markets, the 10-year benchmark Bund was at 103.72 for a bid yield of 5.495 percent, while the DTB September Bund future was 31 basis points higher at 103.32 by the same time.
On Monday, IBIS computer trade was stopped for 90 minutes and the opening of bourse floor trade was delayed for about two hours due to computer network problems.
